name: Spinal Metastases / Metastatic Spinal Cord Compression
definition: Malignant involvement of the spine, with metastatic spinal cord compression representing an oncological emergency because delay can cause permanent neurological injury.

typical: Severe unremitting or progressive spinal pain
Night pain or pain aggravated by straining can occur
Gait disturbance, weakness or sensory symptoms when neural compression develops

redFlags.item: Cancer history plus gait disturbance/difficulty walking
Cancer history plus limb weakness, sensory loss or neurological signs of cord/cauda equina compression

differentials: Cauda equina syndrome from disc disease

investigations.principle: NICE NG234 uses urgent cancer/MSCC pathways for suspected cord compression and defines this as an oncological emergency.
investigations.MRI: Urgent MRI pathway is central when MSCC is suspected; exact timing and whole-spine protocol should follow the local oncology/MSCC pathway.
investigations.stability: Assess spinal stability and immobilization needs according to specialist pathway.

amber: Do not manage suspected MSCC as routine mechanical back pain; neurological signs in a patient with current/past cancer require immediate escalation.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: No Ayurvedic correlation should delay or substitute for the oncological emergency pathway.

patientEducation.summary: Malignant involvement of the spine, with metastatic spinal cord compression representing an oncological emergency because delay can cause permanent neurological injury.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal pain, or cancer-associated neurological symptoms.

sources.title: NG234 Spinal metastases and metastatic spinal cord compression
